translations.literal: Auspicious Rites 1)
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious Rites 1)

sentences.zh: 登極儀授受儀太后垂簾儀親政儀大朝儀常朝儀御門聽政附古太上皇帝三大節朝賀儀太皇太后皇太后皇后三大節朝賀儀

translations.literal: Enthronement rites, transmission and receipt rites, empress dowager curtain administration rites, personal rule rites, grand audience rites, regular audience rites, gate audience for hearing affairs, appended: ancient retired emperor three great festivals congratulatory audience rites, grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress three great festivals congratulatory audience rites
translations.idiomatic: Enthronement rites; transmission and receipt rites; empress-dowager curtain administration; personal rule; grand and regular audiences; gate audiences for hearing affairs—with appended rites for the retired emperor's three great festivals, and for the grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress on their three great festivals

sentences.zh: 大宴儀上尊號徽號儀尊封太妃太嬪儀附冊立中宮儀冊紀嬪儀附主冊皇太子儀太子千秋節附冊諸王儀冊公主附知二曰嘉禮。

translations.literal: Grand banquet rites, honorific title and emblem title rites, ennoblement of grand consort and grand concubine rites, appended investiture of the empress rites, investiture of consorts and concubines rites, appended chief investiture of the crown prince rites, crown prince longevity festival, appended investiture of princes rites, investiture of princesses, appended note two: these are Auspicious Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Grand banquets; bestowal of honorific and emblem titles; ennoblement of grand consorts and grand concubines; investiture of the empress and of consorts and concubines; chief investiture of the crown prince and his longevity festival; investiture of princes and princesses—with a note that all belong to Auspicious Rites.

sentences.zh: 屬於天子者，曰朝會、燕饗、冊命、經筵諸典。

translations.literal: Those belonging to the Son of Heaven are called the canons of court assembly, banquet feasts, investiture patents, and classics lectures.
translations.idiomatic: For the Son of Heaven they comprise court assemblies, banquet feasts, investiture patents, and classics lectures.

sentences.zh: 行於庶人者，曰鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: Those practiced among commoners are called the village drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Among commoners the chief example is the village drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 而婚嫁之禮，則上與下同也。

translations.literal: As for marriage rites, high and low observe them alike.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage rites, however, are observed alike from the throne to the people.

sentences.zh: 周官「以嘉禮親萬民」，體國經野，罔不繇此。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou says, "With auspicious rites draw the myriad people near"; in ordering the state and mapping the wilds, nothing fails to proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou says, "With auspicious rites draw the myriad people near"—in ordering the state and mapping the wilds, nothing is outside their scope.

sentences.zh: 茲舉其大者，附以儀之同者，著於篇。

translations.literal: Here the great items are set forth; where rites are alike, they are appended, and all are recorded in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Here the chief ceremonies are presented; shared procedures are appended, and the whole is set down in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 登極儀清初太祖創業，建元天命，正月朔即位，貝勒、群臣集殿前，按翼序立。

translations.literal: Enthronement rites: In the early Qing the Taizu founded the enterprise, established the era name Tianming, and on the first day of the first month ascended the throne; beile and ministers assembled before the hall and stood in wing order.
translations.idiomatic: Enthronement rites: At the founding of the Qing, Taizu established the Tianming era; on New Year's Day he took the throne, and beile and ministers assembled before the hall and stood in wing order.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御殿，皆跪。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the hall; all knelt.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the hall, all knelt.

sentences.zh: 八大臣出班，跪進上尊號表，侍臣受，跪御前宣讀。

translations.literal: Eight great ministers left the ranks, knelt, and presented the memorial for an honorific title; attendants received it and, kneeling before the throne, read it aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Eight great ministers stepped forward, knelt, and presented the memorial for an honorific title; attendants received it and, kneeling before the throne, read it aloud.

sentences.zh: 帝降座，焚香告天，率貝勒、群臣行禮，三跪九叩，畢，復座，貝勒等各率旗屬慶賀。

translations.literal: The emperor left the seat, burned incense and reported to Heaven, led the beile and ministers in performing the rite of three kneelings and nine kowtows; when finished he resumed the seat, and each beile led his banner followers in congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left his seat, burned incense and reported to Heaven, and led beile and ministers in three kneelings and nine kowtows; when the rite was done he resumed his seat, and each beile led his banner followers in congratulations.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐阼亦如之。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne he did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's accession followed the same rite.

sentences.zh: 天聰十年，改元崇德，建國號曰大清。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tiancong the era name was changed to Chongde and the state title was proclaimed Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 10 the era was changed to Chongde and the state was proclaimed Great Qing.

sentences.zh: 前期誓戒三日，築壇，備鹵簿。

translations.literal: Three days beforehand there was oath and abstinence; an altar was built and the guard of honor prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Three days beforehand the court fasted and abstained; an altar was built and the ceremonial guard prepared.

sentences.zh: 屆日，帝率群臣詣天壇祗告。

translations.literal: On the appointed day the emperor led the ministers to the Altar of Heaven to report reverently.
translations.idiomatic: On the day appointed the emperor led the ministers to the Altar of Heaven for the reverent report.

sentences.zh: 禮成，奉御寶官先行，帝自中階登壇升座，貝勒等三跪九叩。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete the officer bearing the imperial seal went first; the emperor ascended by the central steps, took his seat on the altar, and the beile performed three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished the officer bearing the imperial seal went first; the emperor ascended by the central steps and took his seat on the altar, and the beile performed three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 畢，眾跪，貝勒分左右列。

translations.literal: When finished all knelt; the beile lined up left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When that was done all knelt; the beile formed ranks to left and right.

sentences.zh: 奉寶官跪獻，帝受寶，轉授內院官，群臣行禮如初。

translations.literal: The seal-bearer knelt and presented it; the emperor received the seal and handed it to an Inner Court officer; the ministers performed the rite as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The seal-bearer knelt and presented the seal; the emperor received it and handed it to an Inner Court officer, and the ministers performed the rite as before.

sentences.zh: 畢，皆跪，宣讀官奉滿、蒙、漢三體表文立壇東，以次畢讀，群臣行禮訖，復位，奏樂，駕還宮。

translations.literal: When finished all knelt; the reading officer, holding the memorial in Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese, stood east of the altar and read each in turn; when the ministers' rite was finished they returned to place, music was played, and the imperial procession returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When finished all knelt; the reading officer, holding the trilingual memorial, stood east of the altar and read each text in turn; when the ministers' rite was done they returned to place, music sounded, and the procession returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 翼日帝御殿，群臣表賀，三跪九叩，次執事官行禮如前儀。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor entered the hall; the ministers presented congratulatory memorials with three kneelings and nine kowtows; then the officiating officers performed the rite as in the former protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor entered the hall; ministers presented congratulatory memorials with three kneelings and nine kowtows, and officiating officers then performed the rite as before.

sentences.zh: 於是賜宴，頒赦詔。

translations.literal: Thereupon a banquet was granted and an amnesty edict promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: A banquet was then granted and an amnesty edict promulgated.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖嗣服，遣官告壇、廟如初禮，唯不設鹵簿，不作樂，不賜宴。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Shizu succeeded to the throne; officers were dispatched to report at altar and temple as in the first rite, only without setting out the guard of honor, without music, and without granting a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Shizu succeeded; officers reported at altar and temple as in the first rite, but without the guard of honor, music, or banquet.

sentences.zh: 順治元年十月朔，定鼎燕京，先期太常官除壇壝，司禮監設座案。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month of Shunzhi 1, when the capital was fixed at Yanjing, beforehand the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices cleared the altar enclosure and the Directorate of Ceremonial set seat and tables.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month of Shunzhi 1, when the capital was fixed at Yanjing, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices cleared the altar enclosure beforehand and the Directorate of Ceremonial set seats and tables.

sentences.zh: 屆日，遣官告廟、社，備大駕鹵簿，帝御祭服，出大清門，詣南郊，告天地。

translations.literal: On the day appointed, officers were sent to report at temple and altar; the great imperial guard of honor was prepared; the emperor wore sacrificial robes, went out the Daqing Gate, and proceeded to the southern suburbs to report to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day officers reported at temple and altar; the great imperial guard was prepared; the emperor in sacrificial robes went out the Daqing Gate to the southern suburbs to report to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 禮成，導入天壇東幄次易禮服。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete he was led into the eastern tent at the Altar of Heaven to change into court dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished he was led into the eastern tent at the Altar of Heaven to change into court dress.

sentences.zh: 御座，群臣跪，禮部尚書引大學士一人升自東階，正中北面跪，學士一人自案上奉寶授大學士，祗受，致辭云：「皇帝君臨萬國，諸王文武群臣不勝歡忭。

translations.literal: He took the throne; the ministers knelt; the Minister of Rites led one Grand Secretary up the eastern steps; at the center, facing north, he knelt; one academician took the seal from the table and presented it to the Grand Secretary, who received it reverently and spoke the address: "The emperor rules the myriad states; the princes and civil and military ministers cannot contain their joy."
translations.idiomatic: He took the throne; ministers knelt; the Minister of Rites led one Grand Secretary up the eastern steps to kneel at the center facing north; an academician took the seal from the table and presented it to the Grand Secretary, who received it reverently and said: "The emperor rules the myriad states; princes and civil and military ministers cannot contain their joy."

sentences.zh: 」訖，轉授學士，學士跪受，陳於案，復位。

translations.literal: " When finished he handed it to the academician; the academician knelt to receive it, placed it on the table, and returned to place.
translations.idiomatic: When finished he handed it to the academician; the academician knelt to receive it, placed it on the table, and returned to place.

sentences.zh: 群臣禮畢，駕還宮。

translations.literal: When the ministers' rite was finished the procession returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers' rite was finished the procession returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺官設御案皇極門中，檐東設表案，王、貝勒等序立內金水橋北，文武官序立橋南，俱東西鄉。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments set the imperial table in the center of the Huangji Gate; east of the eaves a table for memorials was set; princes and beile lined up in order north of the Inner Golden Water Bridge and civil and military officials south of the bridge, all facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments set the imperial table in the center of the Huangji Gate; east of the eaves stood the memorial table; princes and beile lined up north of the Inner Golden Water Bridge and officials south of it, all facing east or west.

sentences.zh: 樂作，帝御座則止。

translations.literal: Music began; when the emperor took the throne it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Music began and ceased when the emperor took the throne.

sentences.zh: 鳴鞭。

translations.literal: The whip was sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The whip was sounded.

sentences.zh: 執事官階上行禮畢，就位。

translations.literal: When the officiating officers had performed the rite on the steps they took their places.
translations.idiomatic: Officiating officers performed the rite on the steps and took their places.

sentences.zh: 王率群臣進表，行禮畢，鳴鞭，駕還宮。

translations.literal: The prince led the ministers in presenting memorials; when the rite was finished the whip sounded and the procession returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The prince led ministers in presenting memorials; when the rite was finished the whip sounded and the procession returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 越九日甲子，頒詔如制。

translations.literal: Nine days later, on the jiazi day, an edict was promulgated as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Nine days later, on jiazi day, an edict was promulgated as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 聖祖纘業，分遣官祭告天地、宗社，帝衰服詣几筵行三跪九叩禮，祗告受命。

translations.literal: When Shengzu continued the enterprise, officers were separately dispatched to report at Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple; the emperor in mourning dress went to the mourning couch and performed three kneelings and nine kowtows to report reverently that he had received the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzu continued the enterprise, officers reported at Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple; the emperor in mourning dress went to the mourning couch and performed three kneelings and nine kowtows to report that he had received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 御側殿易禮服，詣太皇太后、皇太后兩宮，各行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: He entered a side hall to change into court dress and proceeded to the palaces of the grand empress dowager and empress dowager, performing three kneelings and nine kowtows at each.
translations.idiomatic: He changed into court dress in a side hall and went to the grand empress dowager and empress dowager, performing three kneelings and nine kowtows at each palace.

sentences.zh: 遂乘輿出乾清門，御中和殿，內大臣等執事官行禮。

translations.literal: Then he took the palanquin out the Gate of Heavenly Purity, entered the Hall of Central Harmony, and inner grand ministers and officiating officers performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode out the Gate of Heavenly Purity to the Hall of Central Harmony, where inner grand ministers and officiating officers performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 復御太和殿，王公百官上錶行禮如儀。

translations.literal: He again entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; princes and officials presented memorials and performed the rite as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: He again entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; princes and officials presented memorials and performed the rite as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 不宣讀，不作樂，不設宴。

translations.literal: There was no public reading, no music, and no banquet.
translations.idiomatic: There was no public reading, no music, and no banquet.

sentences.zh: 王公入，賜茶畢，還宮。

translations.literal: When the princes entered, tea was granted; when finished they returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Princes entered, tea was granted, and they returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 反喪服，就苫次，頒詔。

translations.literal: He put on mourning dress again, went to the mourning shed, and promulgated an edict.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed mourning dress, went to the mourning shed, and promulgated an edict.

sentences.zh: 世宗承大統，一如前儀，惟罷賜茶。

translations.literal: When Shizong received the great succession he followed the same rite, only omitting the granting of tea.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's succession followed the same rite, except that tea was not granted.

sentences.zh: 高宗以後，儲宮嗣立者並同。

translations.literal: From Gaozong onward, when the heir apparent succeeded, all was the same.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong onward, when the heir apparent succeeded, the procedure was the same.

sentences.zh: 授受儀古內禪儀。

translations.literal: Transmission and receipt rites: the ancient inner abdication rite.
translations.idiomatic: Transmission and receipt rites: the ancient inner abdication ceremony.

sentences.zh: 初高宗享國日久，嘗諭年至八十六歲即歸政。

translations.literal: At first Gaozong had long enjoyed the realm and once declared that at eighty-six he would return the government.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong had long ruled and once declared that at eighty-six he would return the government.

sentences.zh: 逮乾隆六十年，詔曰：「自古帝王內禪，非其時怠荒，即其時多故，倉猝授受，禮無可采。

translations.literal: By Qianlong 60 an edict said: "From antiquity when emperors abdicated within, either the time was one of neglect or the time was troubled; a hurried transmission and receipt left no rite worth adopting."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 60 an edict said: "From antiquity, inner abdication was either mistimed through neglect or troubled by events; hurried transmission left no rite worth adopting."

sentences.zh: 今國家全盛，其詳議典禮以聞。

translations.literal: "Now the state is in full prosperity; deliberate fully on the canonical rites and report."
translations.idiomatic: "Now the state is in full prosperity; deliberate fully on the canonical rites and report."

sentences.zh: 」於是諏吉定儲位，以明年為嗣皇帝元年。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an auspicious day was chosen to fix the heir's position, and the next year was made the first year of the succeeding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious days were chosen to fix the heir's position, and the next year became the succeeding emperor's first year.

sentences.zh: 禮臣上儀注。

translations.literal: The ritual officials submitted the protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials submitted the protocol.

sentences.zh: 先期遣官祭告廟、社，屆日所司設御座太和殿。

translations.literal: Beforehand officers were sent to report at temple and altar; on the day the relevant offices set the imperial seat in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand officers reported at temple and altar; on the day the relevant offices set the imperial seat in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 左右幾二，正中寶案，稍南東西肆；

translations.literal: Two tables left and right; at the center a seal table, slightly south, set out east and west;
translations.idiomatic: Two tables left and right; at the center a seal table, set out slightly south to east and west;

sentences.zh: 東楹詔案，西楹表案，南北肆；

translations.literal: east pillar an edict table, west pillar a memorial table, set out north and south;
translations.idiomatic: at the east pillar an edict table, at the west pillar a memorial table, set out north and south;

sentences.zh: 黃案居丹陛中。

translations.literal: a yellow table stood in the middle of the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: a yellow table stood in the middle of the red steps.

sentences.zh: 檻內敷嗣皇帝拜褥。

translations.literal: Within the railing the succeeding emperor's kneeling cushion was spread.
translations.idiomatic: Within the railing the succeeding emperor's kneeling cushion was spread.

sentences.zh: 殿前陳鹵簿，門外步輦。

translations.literal: Before the hall the guard of honor was arrayed; outside the gate the sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: Before the hall the guard of honor was arrayed; outside the gate the sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 午門外五輅、馴象、仗馬、黃蓋、雲盤，檐下設中和韶樂，門外丹陛大樂。

translations.literal: Outside the Meridian Gate the five chariots, trained elephants, ceremonial horses, yellow canopy, and cloud trays; under the eaves Zhonghe ceremonial music; outside the gate Dandi grand music.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Meridian Gate stood the five chariots, trained elephants, ceremonial horses, yellow canopy, and cloud trays; under the eaves Zhonghe ceremonial music; outside the gate Dandi grand music.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士奉傳位詔陳東案，禮部官陳賀表西案，大學士等詣乾清門請寶陳左幾，大學士二人分立兩檐下，王公百官序立。

translations.literal: A Grand Secretariat academician placed the abdication edict on the east table; a Ministry of Rites officer placed the congratulatory memorial on the west table; Grand Secretaries and others went to the Gate of Heavenly Purity to request the seal and place it on the left table; two Grand Secretaries stood one under each eave; princes and officials stood in order.
translations.idiomatic: A Grand Secretariat academician placed the abdication edict on the east table; a Ministry of Rites officer placed the congratulatory memorial on the west; Grand Secretaries fetched the seal from the Gate of Heavenly Purity and set it on the left table; two Grand Secretaries stood under the eaves; princes and officials stood in order.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮、安南、暹羅、廓爾喀使臣列班末。

translations.literal: Envoys from Korea, Annam, Siam, and Gurkha stood at the end of the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Korea, Annam, Siam, and Gurkha stood at the end of the ranks.

sentences.zh: 欽天監官詣乾清門報時，嗣皇帝朝服出毓慶宮，時後扈內大臣二人率侍衛二十人集乾清門外，導引禮部長官二人立門階下，前引大臣十人立殿後階下。

translations.literal: An Astronomical Bureau officer went to the Gate of Heavenly Purity to announce the hour; the succeeding emperor in court dress left the Palace of Cultivation of Youth; afterward two inner grand ministers led twenty guards and assembled outside the Gate of Heavenly Purity; two chief Ministry of Rites officers stood below the gate steps as guides; ten leading ministers stood below the rear hall steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Bureau announced the hour at the Gate of Heavenly Purity; the succeeding emperor in court dress left the Palace of Cultivation of Youth; afterward two inner grand ministers with twenty guards assembled outside the gate; two chief Ministry of Rites officers stood below the gate steps; ten leading ministers below the rear hall steps.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝禮服乘輿出，嗣皇帝從諸臣前引後扈。

translations.literal: The retired emperor in court dress rode out in the palanquin; the succeeding emperor followed, with ministers leading before and escorting behind.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor in court dress rode out; the succeeding emperor followed, with ministers leading before and escorting behind.

sentences.zh: 午門鳴鐘鼓，至殿後降輿。

translations.literal: At the Meridian Gate bells and drums sounded; at the rear of the hall they descended from the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and drums sounded at the Meridian Gate; at the rear of the hall they descended from the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝御中和殿升座，嗣皇帝殿內西鄉立，鴻臚寺官引執事大臣按班，不贊，行九叩禮。

translations.literal: The retired emperor entered the Hall of Central Harmony and ascended the throne; the succeeding emperor stood west inside the hall; the Court of Imperial Entertainments led the officiating ministers by rank without vocal prompts, performing nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor entered the Hall of Central Harmony and ascended the throne; the succeeding emperor stood to the west inside; the Court of Imperial Entertainments led officiating ministers by rank without prompts in nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 侍班者趨出，就外朝位，中和韶樂作，奏元平章。

translations.literal: Those on attendance duty hurried out to outer court positions; Zhonghe ceremonial music played the Yuanping movement.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants hurried to outer court positions; Zhonghe ceremonial music played the Yuanping movement.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝御太和殿，嗣皇帝侍立如初。

translations.literal: The retired emperor entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the succeeding emperor attended standing as before.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the succeeding emperor attended as before.

sentences.zh: 樂止，階下鳴鞭三，丹陛大樂作，奏慶平章。

translations.literal: Music ceased; below the steps the whip sounded thrice; Dandi grand music played the Qingping movement.
translations.idiomatic: Music ceased; the whip sounded thrice below the steps; Dandi grand music played the Qingping movement.

sentences.zh: 嗣皇帝詣拜位立，王公立丹陛上，百官及陪臣立丹墀下，鳴贊官贊「跪」，嗣皇帝率群臣跪。

translations.literal: The succeeding emperor went to the kneeling place and stood; princes stood on the red steps; officials and attendant envoys stood in the courtyard below; the herald officer called "Kneel," and the succeeding emperor led the ministers in kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: The succeeding emperor went to the kneeling place; princes stood on the red steps; officials and envoys in the courtyard below; the herald called "Kneel," and the succeeding emperor led ministers in kneeling.

sentences.zh: 贊「宣表」，宣表官入，奉表至檐下正中跪，大學士二人左右跪，展表，樂止。

translations.literal: The herald called "Proclaim the memorial"; the proclaiming officer entered, carried the memorial to kneel at the center under the eaves; two Grand Secretaries knelt left and right and unfolded the memorial; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called "Proclaim the memorial"; the proclaiming officer carried the memorial to kneel at the center under the eaves; two Grand Secretaries knelt left and right and unfolded it; music ceased.

sentences.zh: 宣訖，還奉原案，退。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished he returned it to the original table and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished he returned it to the original table and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 贊「興」，嗣皇帝退立左旁，西鄉，大學士二人導近御前跪。

translations.literal: The herald called "Rise"; the succeeding emperor withdrew to stand at the left, facing west; two Grand Secretaries guided him to kneel near the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called "Rise"; the succeeding emperor withdrew to the left facing west; two Grand Secretaries guided him to kneel near the throne.

sentences.zh: 左大學士請寶，跪奉太上皇帝，太上皇帝親授嗣皇帝，嗣皇帝跪受，右大學士跪接，陳右幾。

translations.literal: The left Grand Secretary requested the seal, knelt, and presented it to the retired emperor; the retired emperor personally handed it to the succeeding emperor, who knelt to receive it; the right Grand Secretary knelt to take it and placed it on the right table.
translations.idiomatic: The left Grand Secretary requested the seal and presented it to the retired emperor; the retired emperor personally handed it to the succeeding emperor, who knelt to receive it; the right Grand Secretary knelt to take it and placed it on the right table.

sentences.zh: 嗣皇帝詣拜位，樂作，贊「跪，叩，興」，率群臣行九叩禮。

translations.literal: The succeeding emperor went to the kneeling place; music played; the herald called "Kneel, kowtow, rise," and he led the ministers in nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The succeeding emperor went to the kneeling place; music played; the herald called "Kneel, kowtow, rise," and he led ministers in nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 贊「退」，樂止，禮成。

translations.literal: The herald called "Withdraw"; music ceased; the rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The herald called "Withdraw"; music ceased; the rite was complete.

sentences.zh: 鳴鞭如初。

translations.literal: The whip sounded as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The whip sounded as before.

sentences.zh: 中和韶樂作，奏和平章。

translations.literal: Zhonghe ceremonial music played the Heping movement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe ceremonial music played the Heping movement.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝還宮。

translations.literal: The retired emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 內監豫設樂懸，太上皇帝御內殿，公主，福晉，暨皇孫、皇曾元孫未錫爵者，行禮慶賀。

translations.literal: Eunuchs had set the musical stands beforehand; the retired emperor entered the inner hall; princesses, fujin, and imperial grandsons and great-grandsons not yet ennobled performed the rite and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs had set musical stands beforehand; the retired emperor entered the inner hall; princesses, fujin, and imperial grandsons and great-grandsons not yet ennobled performed congratulations.

sentences.zh: 嗣皇帝易禮服，祗俟保和殿暖閣，內閣學士豫奉傳位詔及御寶陳太和殿中案，禮部官奉登極賀表陳東案，扈引者集保和殿外。

translations.literal: The succeeding emperor changed into court dress and waited reverently in the warm pavilion of the Hall of Preserving Harmony; Grand Secretariat academicians had placed the abdication edict and imperial seal on the central table in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; Ministry of Rites officers placed the enthronement congratulatory memorial on the east table; escorts assembled outside the Hall of Preserving Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The succeeding emperor changed into court dress and waited in the warm pavilion of the Hall of Preserving Harmony; Grand Secretariat academicians had placed the abdication edict and seal on the central table in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; Ministry of Rites officers placed the enthronement memorial on the east table; escorts assembled outside the Hall of Preserving Harmony.

sentences.zh: 欽天監報時，嗣皇帝御中和殿，執事者按班行禮，不贊。

translations.literal: The Astronomical Bureau announced the hour; the succeeding emperor entered the Hall of Central Harmony; officiators performed the rite by rank without prompts.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Bureau announced the hour; the succeeding emperor entered the Hall of Central Harmony; officiators performed the rite by rank without prompts.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，嗣皇帝御太和殿登極。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished the succeeding emperor entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished the succeeding emperor entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony to ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 作樂，止樂，宣表，行禮，悉准前式。

translations.literal: Music was played and stopped; the memorial was proclaimed; the rite performed—all exactly as in the former pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Music was played and stopped; the memorial proclaimed; the rite performed—all as in the former pattern.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，退，復位。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished they withdrew and returned to place.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished they withdrew and returned to place.

sentences.zh: 大學士進，奉詔，出中門，授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: A Grand Secretary advanced, received the edict, went out the central gate, and handed it to the Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A Grand Secretary advanced, received the edict, went out the central gate, and handed it to the Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尚書跪受，興，奉置黃案，行三叩禮。

translations.literal: The minister knelt to receive it, rose, placed it on the yellow table, and performed three kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The minister knelt to receive it, rose, placed it on the yellow table, and performed three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 復奉詔陳雲盤，儀制司一人跪受，興，自中道出。

translations.literal: He again received the edict and placed it on the cloud tray; one officer of the Directorate of Ceremonial knelt to receive it, rose, and went out by the central way.
translations.idiomatic: He again received the edict, placed it on the cloud tray; an officer of the Directorate of Ceremonial knelt to receive it, rose, and went out by the central way.

sentences.zh: 禮成，俱退，嗣皇帝還宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete all withdrew; the succeeding emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete all withdrew; the succeeding emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 大學士等詣乾清門送寶，禮部恭鐫詔書頒行。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries and others went to the Gate of Heavenly Purity to return the seal; the Ministry of Rites respectfully carved the edict text and promulgated it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries went to the Gate of Heavenly Purity to return the seal; the Ministry of Rites carved the edict and promulgated it.

sentences.zh: 垂簾儀咸豐十一年，文宗崩，穆宗幼沖嗣位。

translations.literal: Curtain administration rites: In Xianfeng 11 Wenzong died and Muzong succeeded as a child.
translations.idiomatic: Curtain administration rites: In Xianfeng 11 Wenzong died and Muzong succeeded as a child.

sentences.zh: 御史董元醇奏請皇太后暫權朝政，稱旨，命王大臣等議垂簾儀制。

translations.literal: Censor Dong Yuanchun memorialized asking the empress dowager temporarily to hold court authority; the memorial pleased the throne, and princes and great ministers were ordered to deliberate on curtain administration protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dong Yuanchun asked the empress dowager temporarily to hold court authority; the memorial pleased the throne, and princes and great ministers were ordered to draft curtain administration protocol.

sentences.zh: 議上，懿旨猶謂「垂簾非所樂為，唯以時事多艱，王大臣等不能無所稟承，姑允所請」云。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, the empress's rescript still said, "Curtain administration is not what I desire; only because affairs are difficult and the princes and great ministers cannot be without someone to consult, I provisionally grant the request."
translations.idiomatic: When deliberation was submitted, the empress's rescript still said, "Curtain administration is not what I desire; only because affairs are difficult and princes and great ministers cannot be without counsel, I provisionally grant the request."

sentences.zh: 於是仲冬月朔，帝奉兩宮皇太后御養心殿聽政，王公大臣集殿門外，行禮如儀。

translations.literal: Thereupon on the first day of mid-winter the emperor led the two empresses dowager to hear affairs at the Hall of Mental Cultivation; princes and great ministers assembled outside the hall gate and performed the rite as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of mid-winter the emperor led the two empresses dowager to hear affairs at the Hall of Mental Cultivation; princes and great ministers assembled outside the gate and performed the rite as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 凡召見內外臣工，兩宮皇太后、皇帝同御養心殿，太后前垂簾。

translations.literal: Whenever civil and military officials within and without were summoned, the two empresses dowager and the emperor together entered the Hall of Mental Cultivation; before the empresses a curtain was hung.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever officials within and without were summoned, the two empresses dowager and the emperor together entered the Hall of Mental Cultivation; a curtain hung before the empresses.

sentences.zh: 或召某臣進見，議政王、御前大臣番頒之。

translations.literal: When a certain minister was summoned for audience, the prince regent and grand ministers before the throne announced it in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: When a minister was summoned, the prince regent and grand ministers before the throne announced it in rotation.

sentences.zh: 引見外官，則御養心殿前殿，議政王、御前大臣率侍衛等按班分立，太后前垂簾設案，進各員銜名，豫擬諭旨，分別錄注。

translations.literal: When outer officials were presented, they met in the front hall of the Hall of Mental Cultivation; the prince regent and grand ministers led guards to stand by rank; before the empresses a curtain and table were set; each man's title was presented, the rescript drafted beforehand and noted separately.
translations.idiomatic: For outer officials the front hall was used; the prince regent and grand ministers led guards by rank; before the empresses stood curtain and table; titles were presented and rescripts drafted beforehand and noted separately.

sentences.zh: 皇帝前設案，各長官依例進綠頭簽，議政王等奉陳案上，引見如常儀。

translations.literal: Before the emperor a table was set; each chief official presented green-head memorials as usual; the prince regent and others placed them on the table; presentation followed ordinary protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor a table was set; chiefs presented green-head memorials as usual; the prince regent placed them on the table; presentation followed ordinary protocol.

sentences.zh: 皇太后簡單內某名鈐印，已，授王大臣傳旨。

translations.literal: The empress dowager selected a certain name inside and affixed the seal; when finished she handed it to the princes and great ministers to transmit the decree.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager selected a name inside and affixed the seal; when finished she handed it to princes and great ministers to transmit the decree.

sentences.zh: 其臣工請安摺，並具三分以進。

translations.literal: Officials' memorials requesting audience were submitted in three copies.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' audience memorials were submitted in three copies.

sentences.zh: 各省、各路軍事摺報，凡應降諭旨者，議政王等請旨繕擬後，次日呈閱頒行。

translations.literal: Military memorials from each province and route that required imperial rescripts were, after the prince regent and others requested instructions and drafted them, presented for review and promulgation the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Military memorials from provinces and routes requiring rescripts were drafted by the prince regent after requesting instructions, then presented for review and promulgated the next day.

sentences.zh: 唯撰擬文句，仍本帝意，宣示臣工，宜書曰「朕」。

translations.literal: Only in drafting sentences the emperor's intent was still followed; in instructing officials it should be written "I."
translations.idiomatic: Only in drafting sentences the emperor's intent was still followed; in instructing officials the text should read "I."

sentences.zh: 同治十三年，德宗入繼文宗，王公大臣復請兩宮皇太后垂簾，悉准同治初成式。

translations.literal: In Tongzhi 13 Dezong succeeded Wenzong; princes and great ministers again asked the two empresses dowager to administer behind the curtain—all approved according to the Tongzhi initial pattern.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 13 Dezong succeeded Wenzong; princes and great ministers again asked the two empresses dowager to administer behind the curtain—all approved as at the start of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，慈安皇太后薨，慈禧皇太后始專垂簾，制十三年歸政，德宗以時艱尚棘，凡召見、引見，仍升座訓政，設紗屏以障焉。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 6 Empress Dowager Ci'an died; Empress Dowager Cixi alone administered the curtain; the regulation was to return government in thirteen years; Dezong, because affairs were still difficult, for summons and presentations still ascended the throne to instruct government, with gauze screens set as a barrier.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 Empress Dowager Ci'an died; Empress Dowager Cixi alone held the curtain; government was to be returned in thirteen years; because affairs were still difficult, Dezong for summons and presentations still ascended the throne to instruct, with gauze screens as a barrier.

sentences.zh: 親政儀同治十二年正月，兩宮皇太后歸政，穆宗行親政典禮，先期遣告天、地、廟、社，屆日陳皇太后儀駕、皇帝法駕鹵簿，設表案慈寧宮門，檻內敷皇帝拜褥，太和殿內東旁設詔案，東次表案，丹陛中案各一。

translations.literal: Personal rule rites: In the first month of Tongzhi 12 the two empresses dowager returned government; Muzong performed the personal rule ceremony; beforehand officers reported at Heaven, Earth, temple, and altar; on the day the empress dowager's ceremonial guard and the emperor's legal guard were arrayed; a memorial table was set at the Cining Palace gate; within the railing the emperor's kneeling cushion was spread; inside the Hall of Supreme Harmony an edict table was set on the east, an east-side memorial table, and a central courtyard table each one.
translations.idiomatic: Personal rule rites: In the first month of Tongzhi 12 the two empresses dowager returned government; Muzong performed personal rule; beforehand officers reported at Heaven, Earth, temple, and altar; on the day the empress dowager's guard and emperor's legal guard were arrayed; a memorial table at the Cining Palace gate; the emperor's kneeling cushion within the railing; inside the Hall of Supreme Harmony an edict table on the east, an east memorial table, and a central courtyard table.

sentences.zh: 午門外設龍亭、香亭，內閣學士奉皇帝慶賀表文納諸櫝，捧出。

translations.literal: Outside the Meridian Gate a dragon pavilion and incense pavilion were set; a Grand Secretariat academician placed the emperor's congratulatory memorial text in the casket and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Meridian Gate stood a dragon pavilion and incense pavilion; a Grand Secretariat academician placed the emperor's congratulatory memorial in the casket and carried it out.

sentences.zh: 大學士從至永康左門外，大學士接櫝，至慈寧門，升東階，陳案上，退。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries followed to outside the Yongkang Left Gate; a Grand Secretary received the casket and, reaching the Cining Gate, ascended the eastern steps, placed it on the table, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries followed to outside the Yongkang Left Gate; a Grand Secretary received the casket, reached the Cining Gate, ascended the eastern steps, placed it on the table, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 內侍舉案入，庋慈寧宮寶座東，內閣學士奉詔陳殿中黃案，禮部官奉王公百官賀表陳東次黃案。

translations.literal: Inner attendants lifted the table inside and set it east of the throne in the Cining Palace; a Grand Secretariat academician placed the edict on the yellow table in the hall; Ministry of Rites officers placed the congratulatory memorials of princes and officials on the east-side yellow table.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants lifted the table inside and set it east of the throne; a Grand Secretariat academician placed the edict on the yellow table; Ministry of Rites officers placed princes' and officials' congratulatory memorials on the east-side yellow table.

sentences.zh: 凡將軍、提、鎮賀表置龍亭內。

translations.literal: Congratulatory memorials of generals, provincial governors, and commanders were placed in the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Congratulatory memorials of generals, governors, and commanders were placed in the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺官引和碩親王以下，入八分公以上暨蒙古王公等集隆宗門外，不入八分公以下二品大臣以上集長信門外，三品以下集午門外。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments led princes of the first rank and below, nobles of the eighth rank and above, and Mongol princes to assemble outside the Longzong Gate; nobles below the eighth rank and ministers of the second rank and above at the Changxin Gate; third rank and below at the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments led princes of the first rank down, nobles of the eighth rank up, and Mongol princes outside the Longzong Gate; nobles below the eighth rank and ministers of the second rank up at the Changxin Gate; third rank and below at the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 欽天監報時，帝御禮服乘輿出隆宗門，至永康左門外降，王以下隨行，至慈寧門，帝升東階，及門左，西鄉立。

translations.literal: The Astronomical Bureau announced the hour; the emperor in court dress rode out the Longzong Gate, descended outside the Yongkang Left Gate; princes and below followed; reaching the Cining Gate he ascended the eastern steps and, at the left of the gate, stood facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Bureau announced the hour; the emperor in court dress rode out the Longzong Gate and descended outside the Yongkang Left Gate; princes followed; at the Cining Gate he ascended the eastern steps and stood west-facing at the gate's left.

sentences.zh: 日講官四人在西階，東鄉立。

translations.literal: Four lecturers on the western steps stood facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Four lecturers on the western steps stood facing east.

sentences.zh: 前引大臣率侍衛在儀駕末，分左右立。

translations.literal: Leading ministers with guards stood at the end of the ceremonial guard, left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ministers with guards stood at the end of the guard, left and right.

sentences.zh: 皇太后出御慈寧宮，中和樂作，奏豫平章，升座，樂止。

translations.literal: The empress dowager came out to the Cining Palace; Zhonghe music played the Yuping movement; she ascended the throne; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager came out; Zhonghe music played the Yuping movement; she ascended the throne; music ceased.

sentences.zh: 帝就拜位，丹陛樂作，奏益平章。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the kneeling place; Dandi music played the Yiping movement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the kneeling place; Dandi music played the Yiping movement.

sentences.zh: 王公大臣侍衛等循次鄉上立，贊「拜跪」，帝率群臣三跪九拜。

translations.literal: Princes, great ministers, and guards stood in turn facing up; the herald called "Bow and kneel"; the emperor led the ministers in three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, great ministers, and guards stood in turn; the herald called "Bow and kneel"; the emperor led ministers in three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 時西楹下置御史二，鳴贊官二。

translations.literal: At that time two censors were placed below the western pillar; two herald officers.
translations.idiomatic: Two censors stood below the western pillar; two herald officers.

sentences.zh: 儀駕末及午門外御史、禮部官、鳴贊官各二，藉以侍儀。

translations.literal: At the end of the guard and outside the Meridian Gate were two censors, Ministry of Rites officers, and two herald officers each—to assist the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the guard and outside the Meridian Gate were two censors, Ministry of Rites officers, and two herald officers each to assist.

sentences.zh: 永康左門及諸門內外並置鳴贊官，接續外傳。

translations.literal: Outside the Yongkang Left Gate and inside and outside other gates herald officers were placed to relay calls outward.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Yongkang Left Gate and at other gates herald officers relayed calls outward.

sentences.zh: 午門外各官隨同行禮，鳴贊官贊「禮成」，帝復位。

translations.literal: Officials outside the Meridian Gate performed the rite together; the herald called "Rite complete"; the emperor returned to place.
translations.idiomatic: Officials outside the Meridian Gate performed the rite together; the herald called "Rite complete"; the emperor returned to place.

sentences.zh: 王大臣各復位立，皇太后還宮，禮部尚書奏「禮成」，然後帝還宮。

translations.literal: Princes and great ministers each returned to stand; the empress dowager returned to the palace; the Minister of Rites reported "Rite complete"; then the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and great ministers returned to stand; the empress dowager returned; the Minister of Rites reported "Rite complete"; then the emperor returned.

sentences.zh: 俄復出御中和殿，執事官行禮畢，趨出就外朝立，帝御太和殿，樂作，升座，樂止，鳴鞭三，王公百官行禮。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again came out to the Hall of Central Harmony; when officiating officers had finished the rite they hurried out to stand at the outer court; the emperor entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; music played; he ascended the throne; music ceased; the whip sounded thrice; princes and officials performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he entered the Hall of Central Harmony; officiators finished and hurried to the outer court; he entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; music played; he ascended; music ceased; the whip sounded thrice; princes and officials performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 其宣表、頒詔並如前制。

translations.literal: Proclaiming the memorial and promulgating the edict were as in the former regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaiming the memorial and promulgating the edict followed the former regulation.

sentences.zh: 光緒十三年德宗親政仿此。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 13 Dezong's personal rule followed this.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13 Dezong's personal rule followed this.

sentences.zh: 大朝儀天命元年，始行元旦慶賀，制朝儀。

translations.literal: Grand audience rites: In Tianming 1 New Year's congratulations were first held and court audience protocol established.
translations.idiomatic: Grand audience rites: In Tianming 1 New Year's congratulations were first held and court audience protocol established.

sentences.zh: 天聰六年，行新定朝儀，此班朝所繇始，崇德改元，定元旦進表箋及聖節慶賀儀。

translations.literal: In Tiancong 6 the newly fixed court audience was performed—this is where ranked audiences began; when Chongde changed the era, New Year's memorial and felicitation and sacred-day congratulation protocols were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 6 the newly fixed court audience was performed—ranked audiences began here; when Chongde changed the era, New Year's memorial and sacred-day congratulation protocols were fixed.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，定元旦、冬至、萬壽聖節為三大節。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 8 New Year's Day, winter solstice, and Longevity Sacred Festival were fixed as the three great festivals.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 New Year's Day, winter solstice, and the Longevity Sacred Festival were fixed as the three great festivals.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，定正朝會樂章，三大節並設。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 8 the regular court audience music was fixed; for the three great festivals it was fully set.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 regular court audience music was fixed; for the three great festivals it was fully provided.

sentences.zh: 大朝行禮致慶，王以下各官、外籓王子、使臣咸列班次，所司陳鹵簿、樂懸如制。

translations.literal: At the grand audience rite congratulations were offered; princes and officials of every rank and outer-domain princes and envoys all took their ranks; the relevant offices arrayed guard of honor and musical stands as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand audience congratulations were offered; princes, officials of every rank, and outer-domain princes and envoys took their ranks; the relevant offices arrayed guard and music as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 太和殿東具黃案。

translations.literal: East of the Hall of Supreme Harmony a yellow table was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Hall of Supreme Harmony a yellow table was prepared.

sentences.zh: 質明，王、貝勒、貝子集太和門，不入八分公以下官集午門外。

translations.literal: At dawn princes and beile assembled at the Gate of Supreme Harmony; officials below the eighth rank assembled outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn princes and beile assembled at the Gate of Supreme Harmony; officials below the eighth rank outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 禮部奉表置亭內，校尉舁行至午門外陳兩旁，奉表入太和殿列案上。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites placed the memorial in the pavilion; guards carried it to either side outside the Meridian Gate; the memorial was brought into the Hall of Supreme Harmony and set on the table.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites placed the memorial in the pavilion; guards carried it to either side outside the Meridian Gate; it was brought into the hall and set on the table.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚卿引王、貝勒等立丹陛。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments led princes and beile to stand on the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments led princes and beile to the red steps.

sentences.zh: 鳴贊官引群臣暨進表官入兩掖門，序立丹墀。

translations.literal: Herald officers led ministers and memorial-presenting officers in through the side gates to stand in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Herald officers led ministers and memorial presenters through the side gates to the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮、蒙古諸臣自西掖門入，立西班末。

translations.literal: Korean and Mongol ministers entered by the western side gate and stood at the end of the western rank.
translations.idiomatic: Korean and Mongol ministers entered by the western side gate and stood at the end of the western rank.

sentences.zh: 糾儀御史立西檐下東鄉者二人，丹陛、丹墀東西相鄉者各四人，東西班末八人，鳴贊官立殿檐者四人，陛、墀皆如之。

translations.literal: Discipline censors stood two facing east under the western eaves; four east and west on the red steps and courtyard; eight at the ends of the eastern and western ranks; four herald officers under the hall eaves—the same on steps and courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline censors: two facing east under the western eaves; four east and west on steps and courtyard; eight at rank ends; four heralds under the eaves—the same on steps and courtyard.

sentences.zh: 丹陛南階三級，鑾儀衛官六人司鳴鞭。

translations.literal: South of the red steps three levels; six officers of the Imperial Guard sounded the whip.
translations.idiomatic: South of the red steps, three levels; six Imperial Guard officers sounded the whip.

sentences.zh: 欽天監報時，皇帝出御中和殿，執事官行禮畢，趨外朝視事。

translations.literal: The Astronomical Bureau announced the hour; the emperor came out to the Hall of Central Harmony; when officiating officers had finished they hurried to the outer court to conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Bureau announced the hour; the emperor came out to the Hall of Central Harmony; officiators finished and hurried to the outer court.

sentences.zh: 駕出，前導、後扈如儀。

translations.literal: When the procession went out, front guide and rear escort were as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession went out, front guide and rear escort followed protocol.

sentences.zh: 午門鳴鐘鼓，中和樂作，御太和殿，樂止。

translations.literal: At the Meridian Gate bells and drums sounded; Zhonghe music played; he entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At the Meridian Gate bells and drums sounded; Zhonghe music played; he entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; music ceased.

sentences.zh: 內大臣分立前後，侍衛又次其後護守之。

translations.literal: Inner grand ministers stood before and after; guards stood still further behind to protect.
translations.idiomatic: Inner grand ministers stood before and after; guards behind to protect.

sentences.zh: 起居注官四人立西旁金柱後，大學士，學士，講、讀學士，正、少詹事立東檐下。

translations.literal: Four diarists stood behind the western golden pillars; Grand Secretaries, academicians, lecturers and readers, and senior and junior mentors stood under the eastern eaves.
translations.idiomatic: Four diarists stood behind the western pillars; Grand Secretaries, academicians, lecturers, and mentors stood under the eastern eaves.

sentences.zh: 御史、副僉都御史立西檐下，鑾儀衛官贊「鳴鞭」，鳴贊官贊「排班」，王公百官就拜位立跪。

translations.literal: Censors and vice censors-in-chief stood under the western eaves; Imperial Guard officers called "Sound the whip"; herald officers called "Form ranks"; princes and officials went to the kneeling place, stood, and knelt.
translations.idiomatic: Censors stood under the western eaves; guard officers called "Sound the whip"; heralds called "Form ranks"; princes and officials went to the kneeling place and knelt.

sentences.zh: 宣表官奉表出，至殿下正中北鄉跪，大學士二人展表，宣表官宣訖，置原案，丹陛樂作，群臣皆三跪九叩。

translations.literal: The proclaiming officer carried the memorial out to kneel at the center below the hall facing north; two Grand Secretaries unfolded the memorial; when the proclaiming officer finished he placed it on the original table; Dandi music played; all ministers performed three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The proclaiming officer carried the memorial to kneel at the center below facing north; two Grand Secretaries unfolded it; when finished he replaced it; Dandi music played; all performed three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 退，就立原次。

translations.literal: They withdrew and stood in their original places.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew and stood in their original places.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺官引朝鮮等使臣，理籓院官引蒙古使臣就拜次，三跪九叩，丹陛樂作，禮畢，樂止，退立如初。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments led Korean envoys; the Court for the Administration of Domains led Mongol envoys to the kneeling place with three kneelings and nine kowtows; Dandi music played; when the rite was finished music ceased; they withdrew and stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments led Korean envoys; the Domains office led Mongol envoys to kneel with three kneelings and nine kowtows; when finished they withdrew and stood as before.

sentences.zh: 賜坐，群臣暨外臣皆就立處一跪三叩，序坐。

translations.literal: Seats were granted; ministers and outer envoys at their standing places performed one kneeling and three kowtows and took seats in order.
translations.idiomatic: Seats were granted; ministers and envoys at their places performed one kneeling and three kowtows and sat in order.

sentences.zh: 賜茶畢，復鳴鞭三，中和樂作，駕還宮。

translations.literal: When tea was finished the whip sounded thrice again; Zhonghe music played; the procession returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When tea was finished the whip sounded thrice; Zhonghe music played; the procession returned.

sentences.zh: 樂止，群臣退。

translations.literal: Music ceased; the ministers withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Music ceased; ministers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初制，外官元日朝覲，集保和殿前行禮，康熙二十六年後罷。

translations.literal: In the original regulation outer officials on New Year's Day attended court and performed the rite before the Hall of Preserving Harmony; after Kangxi 26 this was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Originally outer officials on New Year's Day attended before the Hall of Preserving Harmony; after Kangxi 26 this was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六年，定行在聖節朝賀行禮。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 6 court congratulations on sacred days while traveling were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 6 congratulations on sacred days while traveling were regulated.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，定大朝百官班次，設立紅漆木牌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the ranks of officials at the grand audience were fixed and red lacquer name boards established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 grand audience ranks were fixed and red lacquer name boards established.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，增置都察院長官二人，科、道三十六人，分立品級山旁整朝序。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year two chief censors of the Censorate and thirty-six censors and remonstrators were added, standing by the rank hills to keep court order.
translations.idiomatic: In year 54 two chief censors and thirty-six censors and remonstrators were added beside the rank hills to keep order.

sentences.zh: 又高宗初年，文三品、武二品以上賜茶，餘惟記注官、外國使臣與焉。

translations.literal: Also in Gaozong's early years civil officials of the third rank and military of the second rank and above were granted tea; the rest only diarists and foreign envoys shared.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozong's reign civil third rank and military second rank and above received tea; others only diarists and foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年罷賜茶。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 2 the granting of tea was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 2 granting tea was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 令甲，元旦、萬壽節午時設宴，冬至節次日受賀。

translations.literal: By regulation, on New Year's Day and Longevity Festival banquets were set at noon; on winter solstice congratulations were received the next day.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation New Year's and Longevity banquets were at noon; winter solstice congratulations came the next day.

sentences.zh: 萬壽節先謁太廟，次詣皇太后宮行禮，畢，受賀。

translations.literal: On Longevity Festival the ancestral temple was visited first, then the empress dowager's palace to perform the rite; when finished congratulations were received.
translations.idiomatic: On Longevity Festival the ancestral temple was visited first, then the empress dowager's palace; when finished congratulations were received.

sentences.zh: 直省文武官值三大節，俱設香案，朝服望闕行禮，滿、蒙、漢軍分兩翼，漢官分文東武西。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of direct provinces on the three great festivals all set incense tables, faced the palace in court dress, and performed the rite; Manchu, Mongol, and Han banners formed two wings; Han officials divided civil east and military west.
translations.idiomatic: Direct-province officials on the three great festivals set incense tables and faced the palace in court dress; Manchu, Mongol, and Han banners formed two wings; Han officials divided civil east, military west.

sentences.zh: 常朝儀太祖丙辰建元後，益勤國政，五日一視朝，焚香告天，宣讀古來嘉言懿行及成敗興廢所由，訓誡臣民，然未垂為定制也。

translations.literal: Regular audience rites: After the Taizu established the era in bingchen he grew still more diligent in government, viewing court every five days, burning incense and reporting to Heaven, reading aloud ancient fine words and deeds and the causes of rise and fall, instructing subjects—yet this was not yet fixed as permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Regular audience rites: After Taizu established the era in bingchen he grew more diligent, holding court every five days, burning incense, reporting to Heaven, and reading ancient exemplars and causes of rise and fall to instruct subjects—yet this was not yet permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 崇德初，始定儀注，設大駕鹵簿，王以下各官朝服，俟帝出宮，樂作。

translations.literal: Early in Chongde the protocol was first fixed; the great imperial guard was set out; princes and officials wore court dress and waited for the emperor to leave the palace; music played.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongde protocol was fixed; the great guard was set out; princes and officials in court dress waited; music played.

sentences.zh: 御殿，升座，樂止。

translations.literal: He entered the hall, ascended the throne; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the hall and ascended the throne; music ceased.

sentences.zh: 賜坐，諸臣各依班次，一叩就座。

translations.literal: Seats were granted; each minister by rank performed one kowtow and took his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Seats were granted; each minister by rank performed one kowtow and sat.

sentences.zh: 部、院官出班奏事畢，駕還宮。

translations.literal: When ministry and court officials had reported affairs the procession returned.
translations.idiomatic: When ministries and courts had reported the procession returned.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，給事中魏象樞言：「故事有朔、望朝，有早朝、晚朝、內朝、外朝，今縱不能如往制，請一月三朝，以副厲精圖治至意。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 9 Remonstrator Wei Xiangsu said: "Formerly there were new- and full-moon audiences, early and late audiences, inner and outer audiences; even if we cannot match the old system, let there be three audiences a month to fulfill the intent of striving to govern well."
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 Remonstrator Wei Xiangsu said: "Formerly there were new- and full-moon, early, late, inner, and outer audiences; even if we cannot match antiquity, let there be three audiences a month to fulfill striving to govern."

sentences.zh: 」楊簧亦言：「舊例百官每月十一朝，似太繁數，今每日入朝奏事，較十一朝不為少，應定每月初五、十五、二十五日行朝參禮。

translations.literal: " Yang Huang also said: "The old rule had officials attend court eleven times a month, which seems too frequent; now daily attendance to report affairs is no less than eleven times; let the first, fifteenth, and twenty-fifth of each month be fixed for court attendance rites."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huang also said: "The old rule was eleven audiences a month—too frequent; daily reporting is no less; let the 1st, 15th, and 25th be fixed for attendance."

sentences.zh: 」自是遂定逢五視朝制。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the rule of viewing court on days ending in five was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon viewing court on fives was fixed.

sentences.zh: 尋定見朝、辭朝、謝恩各官，俱常朝日行禮。

translations.literal: Soon audiences for presentation, farewell audiences, and gratitude audiences were all fixed for regular audience days.
translations.idiomatic: Soon presentation, farewell, and gratitude audiences were fixed for regular audience days.

sentences.zh: 帝御太和殿，引見畢，賜坐賜茶，悉准常儀。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; after presentations seats and tea were granted—all as in the regular protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the Hall of Supreme Harmony; after presentations seats and tea followed regular protocol.

sentences.zh: 如是日不御殿，各官行禮午門外。

translations.literal: If on that day he did not enter the hall, each official performed the rite outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: If he did not enter the hall that day, officials performed the rite outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 外籓來朝暨貢使，亦常朝日行禮，如速返，則不拘朝期，即赴午門行禮，外官應速赴任者亦然。

translations.literal: Outer-domain audiences and tribute envoys also performed on regular audience days; if they must return quickly they were not bound to the audience schedule but went at once to the Meridian Gate; outer officials due to hurry to post were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Outer audiences and tribute envoys used regular days; if they must return quickly they went at once to the Meridian Gate; outer officials hurrying to post likewise.

sentences.zh: 又定常朝御殿，王公入殿中旁坐如次。

translations.literal: It was also fixed that at regular audiences princes sat beside the throne in the hall by rank.
translations.idiomatic: It was also fixed that at regular audiences princes sat in the hall beside the throne by rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，定公、侯、伯以下各官為六班，按次列坐，後復改為九班。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 8 dukes, marquises, and earls down were made six shifts seated in order; later this was changed to nine shifts.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 nobles down to earls were six seated shifts; later nine shifts.

sentences.zh: 九年，諭都察院糾察王大臣失儀。

translations.literal: In year 9 the Censorate was ordered to discipline princes and great ministers for ritual lapses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the Censorate was ordered to discipline princes and great ministers for lapses.

sentences.zh: 二十年，置常朝糾儀御史及司員。

translations.literal: In year 20 regular audience discipline censors and clerks were established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 regular audience discipline censors and clerks were established.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，遣侍衛四人監察朝班，定視朝日天未明，鴻臚寺官二人引左右翼官入西掖門依班坐。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 2 four guards were sent to supervise the court ranks; on audience days before dawn two Court of Imperial Entertainments officers led left- and right-wing officials in the western side gate to sit by rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 four guards supervised ranks; before dawn on audience days two Entertainments officers led wing officials through the western side gate to sit by rank.

sentences.zh: 鼓嚴，起立聽贊，自仗南引進，整齊班列，行禮如儀。

translations.literal: When the drum sounded sternly they rose to hear the herald; from south of the guard they were led in, ranks aligned, and the rite performed as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: When the drum sounded they rose; from south of the guard they were led in, ranks aligned, and the rite performed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，敕大小各官依內廷官例，黎明坐班。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong all great and small officials were ordered to sit on duty at dawn by inner-court example.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong all officials were ordered to sit on duty at dawn by inner-court example.

sentences.zh: 十六年，諭部院大臣董率庶僚，常朝按期赴班，毋曠闕。

translations.literal: In year 16 ministry and court great ministers were ordered to lead subordinates so that regular audiences were attended on schedule without absence.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 great ministers were ordered to lead subordinates to attend regular audiences without absence.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，更定朝制，凡新除授各官，鴻臚寺列銜名交內閣，屆日禮部尚書、鴻臚卿請駕御殿，導各官謝恩行禮，王公百官侍鹵簿後。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 9 the audience system was revised: for each newly appointed official the Court of Imperial Entertainments listed titles and gave them to the Grand Secretariat; on the day the Minister of Rites and the Court director requested the emperor to enter the hall and led each official to perform gratitude; princes and officials attended behind the guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 the system was revised: for new appointments the Entertainments Court listed titles to the Grand Secretariat; on the day the Minister of Rites and director requested the hall and led gratitude; princes and officials attended behind the guard.

sentences.zh: 不御殿，文武官則坐班午門外。

translations.literal: If he did not enter the hall, civil and military officials sat on duty outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: If he did not enter the hall, officials sat on duty outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 其時刻，春冬以辰正，夏秋以卯正，遇雨雪及國忌則免。

translations.literal: The hour: spring and winter at chen proper, summer and autumn at mao proper; on rain, snow, or national mourning it was excused.
translations.idiomatic: Hours: spring and winter at chen proper, summer and autumn at mao proper; rain, snow, or national mourning excused it.

sentences.zh: 坐班日，鴻臚寺官按翼定位，王公集太和門外，東西各二班，百官集午門外，東西各九班，糾儀御史吏、禮司員各四人，分列班首末，並西面北上。

translations.literal: On sitting-duty days Entertainments officers placed by wing; princes assembled outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, two ranks east and west; officials outside the Meridian Gate, nine ranks east and west; four discipline censor clerks each from Personnel and Rites at head and tail, all facing west north-up.
translations.idiomatic: On sitting-duty days officers placed by wing; princes outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony in two ranks; officials outside the Meridian Gate in nine ranks; four discipline clerks at head and tail, facing west north-up.

sentences.zh: 屆時吏、禮司員受職名，糾儀官環班稽察，復位坐。

translations.literal: At the hour Personnel and Rites clerks received duty names; discipline officers circled the ranks to inspect and returned to sit.
translations.idiomatic: At the hour clerks received duty names; discipline officers circled ranks, inspected, and sat again.

sentences.zh: 有間，以次出。

translations.literal: After a while they left in order.
translations.idiomatic: After a while they left in order.

sentences.zh: 御門聽政儀，清初定制，每日聽政，必御正門，九卿科道齊集啟奏，率以為常。

translations.literal: Gate audience for hearing affairs: In the early Qing it was fixed that daily hearing of affairs must be at the main gate; the Nine Ministers and censors assembled to report—all took this as constant.
translations.idiomatic: Gate audience for hearing affairs: Early Qing fixed that daily hearing must be at the main gate; Nine Ministers and censors assembled to report—as constant practice.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，始定御門典禮，凡部院所進本有未經奉旨者，摺本下內閣，積若干，傳旨某日御門辦事。

translations.literal: Early in Yongzheng the gate audience canon was first fixed: whenever ministries submitted memorials not yet decreed, folded memorials went to the Grand Secretariat; when several accumulated, an edict fixed a day to conduct affairs at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng gate audience canon was fixed: undecreed ministry memorials accumulated in the Grand Secretariat; when several piled up, an edict fixed a gate-audience day.

sentences.zh: 是日，乾清門正中設御榻、黼扆、本案一。

translations.literal: On that day at the center of the Gate of Heavenly Purity an imperial couch, embroidered screen, and main table were set.
translations.idiomatic: That day at the center of the Gate of Heavenly Purity stood couch, screen, and main table.

sentences.zh: 黎明，部院奏事大臣暨陪奏官屬畢集庭內。

translations.literal: At dawn reporting ministers of ministries and courts and attendant officials all assembled in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn reporting ministers and attendants assembled in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 帝升座，侍衛左右立，記注官升西階，部院官升東階，各就列跪，尚書前，侍郎後，陪奏官又後。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the throne; guards stood left and right; diarists ascended the western steps; ministry officials ascended the eastern steps and knelt in rank—ministers before, vice-ministers after, attendants still after.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended; guards stood left and right; diarists on the western steps; ministry officials on the eastern steps knelt by rank—ministers before, vice-ministers after, attendants last.

sentences.zh: 尚書一人奉本匣折旋而進，詣本案前，跪陳於案，興，少退，趨東楹，轉入班首。

translations.literal: One minister carried the memorial casket, turned and advanced to the main table, knelt and placed it on the table, rose, withdrew slightly, hurried to the eastern pillar, and turned into the head of the rank.
translations.idiomatic: One minister carried the casket, turned to the main table, knelt and placed it, rose, withdrew, hurried to the eastern pillar, and entered the head of the rank.

sentences.zh: 跪，口奏某事，畢，興，少退，率屬循階左降。

translations.literal: He knelt, orally reported the item, rose, withdrew slightly, and led his subordinates down the steps to the left.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt, reported the item, rose, withdrew, and led subordinates down the steps left.

sentences.zh: 其奏事次序，戶、禮、兵、工四部輪班首上，三法司直第三班，吏部直第六班，宗人府則列部院前，翰詹科道及九卿會奏則居部院後，各依班進奏如初。

translations.literal: The reporting order: Revenue, Rites, War, and Works rotated the lead; the three judicial offices were always the third shift; Personnel always the sixth; the Imperial Clan Court stood before the ministries; Hanlin, censors, and joint memorials of the Nine Ministers stood after, each reporting as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Order: Revenue, Rites, War, Works rotated lead; three judicial offices third shift; Personnel sixth; Imperial Clan before ministries; Hanlin, censors, and Nine Ministers' joint memorials after—each reporting as at first.

sentences.zh: 至吏部奏事，兼帶領各部番直司員八人，引見畢，始退。

translations.literal: When Personnel reported it also led eight rotating clerks of each ministry; after presentations they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Personnel reported it also led eight rotating clerks; after presentations they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 內閣侍讀學士二人升東階，詣案前跪，舉本匣，興，退。

translations.literal: Two Grand Secretariat reader-academicians ascended the eastern steps, went before the table, knelt, lifted the casket, rose, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Two reader-academicians ascended the eastern steps, knelt before the table, lifted the casket, rose, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 翰詹科道暨侍衛俱退。

translations.literal: Hanlin, censors, and guards all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin, censors, and guards withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時欽派讀本滿學士一人，奉摺本匣升東階，折旋而退，大學士從，依班次跪。

translations.literal: At that time one appointed Manchu academician read folded memorials; bearing the folded casket he ascended the eastern steps, turned, and withdrew; Grand Secretaries followed and knelt by rank.
translations.idiomatic: One appointed Manchu academician read folded memorials, bearing the casket up the eastern steps, turning and withdrawing; Grand Secretaries followed and knelt by rank.

sentences.zh: 記注官少進東鄉立，奉匣學士詣案前跪啟匣，取摺本依次啟奏，帝降旨宣答。

translations.literal: The diarist advanced slightly facing east; the academician bearing the casket knelt before the table, opened it, and read folded memorials in order; the emperor issued edicts in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The diarist advanced facing east; the academician knelt, opened the casket, read folded memorials in order; the emperor replied.

sentences.zh: 大學士等承旨訖，興，自東階降，記注官自西階降。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretaries had received the edicts they rose and descended the eastern steps; the diarist descended the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries received edicts, rose, descended east; the diarist descended west.

sentences.zh: 駕還宮。

translations.literal: The procession returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The procession returned.

sentences.zh: 奏事時，令翰林官記注，自順治二年始。

translations.literal: During reporting Hanlin officers were ordered to record—from Shunzhi 2.
translations.idiomatic: During reporting Hanlin were ordered to record—from Shunzhi 2.

sentences.zh: 先是奏事春夏以卯正，秋冬以辰初。

translations.literal: Previously reporting was at mao proper in spring-summer and chen initial in autumn-winter.
translations.idiomatic: Previously reporting was mao proper spring-summer, chen initial autumn-winter.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十一年，命展御門晷刻，春夏改辰初，秋冬辰正。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 21 the gate-audience hour was extended: spring-summer changed to chen initial, autumn-winter to chen proper.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 gate-audience hours were extended: spring-summer to chen initial, autumn-winter to chen proper.

sentences.zh: 越二年，御史衛執蒲請以五日或二三日為期，聖祖諭：「政治務在精勤，始終不宜有間。

translations.literal: Two years later Censor Wei Zhipu asked that the period be every five or two-three days; Shengzu said: "In government one must be precise and diligent from start to finish; there should be no interval."
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Censor Wei Zhipu asked five- or two-three-day intervals; Shengzu said: "Government requires precision and diligence throughout; there should be no interval."

sentences.zh: 」二十五年，置科道各二人侍班，列起居注官上。

translations.literal: In year 25 two censors and remonstrators each attended on duty, standing above the diarists.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 two censors and remonstrators attended on duty above the diarists.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，省起居注官，其侍班翰林，令啟奏摺本時即退。

translations.literal: In year 27 diarists were reduced; attending Hanlin, when folded memorials were read, were ordered to withdraw at once.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 diarists were reduced; attending Hanlin withdrew when folded memorials were read.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，復設起居注官，增二人。

translations.literal: Early in Yongzheng diarists were restored and two more added.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng diarists were restored and two added.

sentences.zh: 又令編檢四人侍班，列科道上。

translations.literal: Also four compilers and revisers were ordered on duty, standing above the censors.
translations.idiomatic: Four compilers and revisers were ordered on duty above censors.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，命修撰、編、檢依科道例，懸數珠，肅朝儀。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 2 compilers and revisers were ordered by censor example to wear prayer beads and keep court decorum.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 compilers and revisers wore prayer beads by censor example to keep decorum.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十八年，諭宣本承旨時，御前大臣及侍衛毋退，著為令。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 18 an edict said that when reading memorials and receiving edicts, grand ministers before the throne and guards must not withdraw—made regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 an edict said that when reading memorials and receiving edicts, grand ministers and guards must not withdraw—made regulation.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝三大節朝賀儀嘉慶元年，高宗傳位仁宗，尊為太上皇帝，定朝賀儀。

translations.literal: Retired emperor three great festivals congratulatory audience rites: In Jiaqing 1 Gaozong transmitted the throne to Renzong and was honored as retired emperor; congratulatory audience rites were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Retired emperor three great festivals congratulatory audience: In Jiaqing 1 Gaozong abdicated to Renzong and was honored retired emperor; congratulatory rites were fixed.

sentences.zh: 屆日陳法駕、鹵簿、樂懸如授受儀，太和殿設三案，表亭舁至午門，慶賀表文陳東案，筆硯陳西案。

translations.literal: On the day the legal guard, ceremonial escort, and musical stands were arrayed as in transmission rites; three tables were set in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the congratulatory memorial pavilion was carried to the Meridian Gate; congratulatory text on the east table, writing implements on the west.
translations.idiomatic: That day legal guard, escort, and music were as in transmission rites; three tables in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the congratulatory pavilion at the Meridian Gate; text east, writing implements west.

sentences.zh: 質明，王公百官朝服，外國使臣服本國服，集闕下。

translations.literal: At dawn princes and officials in court dress; foreign envoys in their national dress assembled below the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn princes and officials in court dress; foreign envoys in national dress below the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇帝禮服，俟保和殿暖閣。

translations.literal: The emperor in court dress waited in the warm pavilion of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in court dress waited in the warm pavilion of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝乘輿出，至太和殿北階降，中和韶樂作，奏元平章，御殿升座，樂止。

translations.literal: The retired emperor rode out, descended at the north steps of the Hall of Supreme Harmony; Zhonghe music played the Yuanping movement; he entered the hall and ascended; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor rode out and descended at the north steps; Zhonghe played Yuanping; he entered and ascended; music ceased.

sentences.zh: 帝殿內西鄉立，鳴鞭三，贊「排班」，丹陛大樂作，奏慶平章。

translations.literal: The emperor stood west inside the hall; the whip sounded thrice; the herald called "Form ranks"; Dandi grand music played the Qingping movement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stood west inside; the whip thrice; "Form ranks"; Dandi played Qingping.

sentences.zh: 帝就拜位，北鄉，時鴻臚官分引群臣暨外使肅班立，贊「進」，贊「跪，叩，興」。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the kneeling place facing north; Entertainments officers led ministers and envoys to stand in ranks; the herald called "Advance," then "Kneel, kowtow, rise."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at the kneeling place facing north; Entertainments led ministers and envoys; "Advance," then "Kneel, kowtow, rise."

sentences.zh: 帝率群臣行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: The emperor led the ministers in three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led ministers in three kneelings and nine kowtows.
